definitions.explanation: A luminous point in the night sky.

examples.japanese: {流れ星|ながれぼし}を{見|み}た。
{夜空|よぞら}に{星|ほし}がたくさん{見|み}える。
examples.english: Many stars are visible in the night sky.

examples.japanese: {田舎|いなか}では{都会|とかい}より{星|ほし}がよく{見|み}える。
examples.english: Stars are more visible in the countryside than in the city.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}、{父|ちち}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{星|ほし}を{見|み}るのが{好|す}きだった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I liked watching the stars together with my father.

notes:
{星|ほし} refers primarily to stars visible in the night sky, not planets in scientific contexts.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {星|ほし}を{見|み}る: to look at stars
- {星|ほし}が{出|で}る: stars come out
- {星|ほし}が{輝|かがや}く: stars shine
- {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}: shooting star
- {星空|ほしぞら}: starry sky

COMPOUNDS:
- {星座|せいざ}: constellation
- {一番星|いちばんぼし}: first star of evening
- {北極星|ほっきょくせい}: North Star

FIGURATIVE USE:
{星|ほし} also means rating stars ({三|み}つ{星|ぼし} = three stars) and can refer to someone's destiny or fate in literary contexts.

SCIENCE NOTE:
In astronomy, {恒星|こうせい} (fixed star) is the technical term, while {惑星|わくせい} refers to planets.
